title: Magnet hooks for the cabin
product: FINDMAG 10-pack cruise magnetic hooks, 50 lb
short: Cruise cabin walls are steel. Hooks turn the walls into closet space.
intro: Cruise cabins are small and the walls and ceiling are steel. Everybody who has cruised before will tell you to bring magnet hooks. I had never cruised, so I believed them and bought three different sets.
This is the 10-pack I would buy again: strong enough for a wet swimsuit, a lanyard, a hat, a bag, and the kids' stuff off the floor.

p: I didn't know how strong they needed to be, so I got a 30 lb set, this 50 lb set, and a couple of 80 lb heavy-duty ones. You don't need all three. If you only buy one, buy this one. The heavy ones are for a backpack or a bag of wet towels.
Ten covers a family. Put a couple of the strong ones by the door for lanyards so you grab them on the way out.

title: Heavy-duty magnet hooks
product: Buelkmag 80 lb+ magnetic hooks
short: The strong ones. For a backpack or a bag of wet towels on the cabin wall.
intro: These are the overkill version of the magnet hooks. I got them for anything heavy: the backpack, the beach bag, wet towels by the bathroom.
If you are buying one set of hooks, buy the 50 lb ten-pack instead. Add these if you have a big bag you want off the floor.

p: Strong magnets pinch fingers. Keep them away from the four-year-old.

title: The lighter magnet hooks
product: FINDMAG 30 lb magnetic hooks, 10-pack
short: Good for lanyards, hats, and light stuff. The 50 lb set covers more.
intro: This is the first set of magnet hooks I bought, before I decided to also get a stronger set. They are fine for hats, lanyards, a light jacket, and keeping the kids' things off the floor.
If you are choosing between this and the 50 lb ten-pack, get the 50.

title: Lanyards for the ship cards
product: 6-pack cruise lanyards with breakaway clasp and card holder
short: Your Sail & Sign card is your room key and your wallet. Wear it.
intro: On Carnival your Sail & Sign card opens your cabin, pays for everything, and gets you on and off the ship. You will use it constantly. A lanyard means you never dig for it, and the kids can't lose theirs.
Six in a pack covered our family of four with two spares.

p: The cards were waiting for us at our cabin door when we boarded, not handed to us at the terminal. So the lanyards go in your carry-on, not the checked bag.
Get breakaway clasps for kids. Get a clear holder so the card can be scanned without taking it out.

title: Cruise-approved power strip
product: Non-surge power strip, 2 USB-C, 2 USB-A, 3 outlets
short: Cabins have almost no outlets. Surge protectors are banned. This is the kind they allow.
intro: Cruise cabins have very few outlets, and we had four people with phones, a tablet, and a watch. Cruise lines ban surge protectors because of the ship's wiring, so you want a non-surge strip like this one.
One plug in the wall turns into seven.

p: Make sure the listing says non-surge. Security can pull a regular surge protector out of your bag. Bring your own cables; the strip is just the ports.

title: Magnetic night light for the cabin
product: 2-pack motion-sensor LED night light, USB rechargeable, magnetic
short: A cruise cabin with the lights off is pitch black. With two little kids, somebody is getting up at night.
intro: A cruise cabin with the lights off is darker than any room in your house. With a four-year-old and a six-year-old, somebody is getting up at night. The motion sensor light sticks to the steel wall by the bathroom and comes on only when someone moves.
Two in the pack: one by the bathroom, one by the beds.

p: Charge both before you leave home. They are USB rechargeable, so they go on the power strip during the day if they run low.

title: Over-the-door organizer
product: Amazon Basics 24-pocket mesh hanging shoe organizer
short: Not for shoes. Sunscreen, chargers, meds, hair ties, the kids' little things.
intro: This is the single best cabin tip I got before we left. Hang it on the bathroom door and all the small stuff that would cover the counter goes in a pocket: sunscreen, toothbrushes, chargers, medicine, hair stuff, sunglasses.
Mesh pockets, so you can see what is where.

p: Twenty-four pockets was more than we needed, but it hangs flat and packs flat. The hooks fit over a standard cabin door.

title: Towel bands for the deck chairs
product: Cruise On towel bands, 4-pack
short: Keeps your towel on the lounge chair when the wind picks up on deck.
intro: The pool deck on a ship is windy. A towel on a lounge chair goes flying the minute you stand up. These stretch around the chair and hold the towel down.
I bought these and a set of clips so I'd have both.

p: Four in a pack, one per chair. Carnival provides the pool towels, so you only bring the bands, not the towels.

title: Towel clips
product: Core Clips heavy-duty beach towel clips for cruise chairs
short: The other way to hold a towel down. Also handy on the beach in Bermuda.
intro: Same job as the towel bands: keep the towel on the chair. Clips also work on a beach chair, a stroller, or a balcony rail for a drying swimsuit.
If you are only buying one, I'd take the bands for the ship and the clips for the beach day.

title: Wet bag for swimsuits
product: Bumkins waterproof wet bag
short: Wet swimsuits go in here, not in the backpack with the phone.
intro: Between the pool deck, the beach in Bermuda, and two kids, something is always wet. The wet bag keeps a soaked suit from ruining everything else in the bag.
Zips shut, washable, packs flat. One per kid is not a bad idea.

title: Travel laundry bags
product: 2-pack large waterproof travel laundry bags with handle
short: Seven nights with kids means a lot of dirty clothes. Keep them separate.
intro: Dirty clothes go in the bag, the bag goes in the closet, and the cabin stays livable. On the last night you pack the clean stuff and carry the bag.
Carnival Pride has self-service laundry rooms if you need them, but the goal is to not need them.

title: Mesh laundry bags
product: Mesh laundry bags, 24 x 36, drawstring
short: The big mesh ones. Good for beach stuff that needs to dry out.
intro: I bought these alongside the waterproof laundry bags. The mesh lets wet things breathe, so sandy, damp beach gear doesn't get funky on the way home.
Also an easy way to carry pool stuff up and down the decks.

title: Mineral sunscreen for the family
product: Thinkbaby SPF 50+ mineral sunscreen, 6 oz
short: Zinc oxide, water resistant, SPF 50. Bermuda sun is no joke.
intro: I stood in Target comparing sunscreens and then checked the EWG guide. The short version: mineral sunscreen with zinc oxide, SPF 30 to 50, no oxybenzone, lotion instead of spray. This one fit.
A week of pool days and a beach day in Bermuda for four people. Bring more than you think.

p: Sunscreen on the ship and in Bermuda costs a lot more than at home. Two full bottles for a family of four for a week is about right. Reapply every two hours and after swimming.

title: Sunscreen stick for the kids' faces
product: ATTITUDE Kids mineral sunscreen stick, SPF 50, EWG Verified
short: A stick is the only way to get sunscreen on a six-year-old's nose and ears.
intro: Lotion on a kid's face turns into a fight. A stick goes on the nose, cheeks, and ears in ten seconds.
EWG Verified, zinc oxide. It goes in a pocket of the over-the-door organizer so it's always by the door.

title: Motion sickness bands
product: LYJEE acupressure motion sickness wristbands
short: Cheap insurance for the first night out of Baltimore.
intro: I had never been on a cruise, so I had no idea if I'd get seasick. These were seven dollars. Worst case they do nothing; best case you don't lose a night of the trip.
Pack real motion sickness medicine too (Dramamine or Bonine) even if you never get sick in a car.

p: The ship's medical center sells motion sickness pills, but at ship prices. Bring your own from home.

title: Swim trunks with pockets
product: Amazon Essentials men's swim trunks, mesh lining, pockets
short: A second pair means one is always dry. Pockets hold the cruise card.
intro: On a cruise you are in the water most days. Two pairs of trunks means you are never putting on a cold wet pair in the morning.
Pockets matter: the Sail & Sign card goes in one when you don't want the lanyard at the pool.

title: Baby powder for sand
product: Johnson's cornstarch baby powder with aloe
short: Old beach trick: powder takes wet sand right off skin before it goes in the bag.
intro: Bermuda beaches have that pink sand and it sticks to everything. Rub baby powder on sandy feet and legs and the sand falls off. It's the one trick every beach parent should know.
Small bottle, lives in the beach bag.

title: Kids' shampoo and body wash
product: The Honest Company 2-in-1 baby shampoo and body wash, fragrance-free
short: Carnival cabins have a shampoo and body wash dispenser in the shower. It's basic. The kids got their own.
intro: One of my first questions before the cruise was whether I needed to bring shampoo. The cabin shower has a dispenser with shampoo and body wash, so adults can get by. For the kids we brought this one so there were no surprises.
Travel size would have been plenty for a week.

title: Choose Your Own Adventure books for the kids
product: Choose Your Own Adventure Jr. (Bubble Town, Your Baby Unicorn, The Lake Monster Mystery)
short: Sea days are long. Books with choices kept a six-year-old busy on the balcony.
intro: There are two full sea days on a Baltimore to Bermuda cruise. My daughter is a great reader, and I wanted her to have something on the balcony that wasn't a screen. Choose-your-path books are the kind she will read twice.
I ordered three. Bubble Town, Your Baby Unicorn, and The Lake Monster Mystery. One per sea day plus a spare.

p: Your Baby Unicorn and The Lake Monster Mystery are the same series. We also brought What Should Darla Do?, a picture book about making choices, for the four-year-old.

title: What Should Darla Do?
product: What Should Darla Do? (The Power to Choose series)
short: A picture book about choices. Packed it for the four-year-old.
intro: A picture book where Darla has to make choices and you see what happens. Good for a four-year-old who is not reading yet but wants to be part of what the six-year-old is doing.
Light, flat, and easy to pack.

title: A 10-foot USB-C cable
product: HOTUTUKI 10 ft USB-A to USB-C 2-in-1 cable
short: The outlet is never where the bed is. A long cable fixes that in a cabin and a hotel.
intro: Cruise cabin outlets are by the desk, not the bed. A ten-foot cable reaches from the power strip to the nightstand so your phone charges where you sleep.
I'd pack two: one for each side of the bed.

title: 128GB flash drive
product: Aiibe 128GB USB flash drive
short: Bought it the week before the cruise to unload phone photos and videos.
intro: A week of trip photos and videos fills a phone fast. A cheap flash drive is a place to dump them without paying for ship Wi-Fi to upload to the cloud.
Nothing fancy. It works.

title: LeapFrog Little Office Learning Center
product: LeapFrog Little Office Learning Center, green
short: A pretend office for a little kid: keyboard, phone, calendar, and it talks. My video shows the best way to use it.
intro: A little desk-shaped toy with a keyboard, a phone, a calendar wheel, and buttons that teach letters, numbers, and days of the week.
I made a video about the best way to use it, because there is more in there than the box shows.

p: Two to five years old. It talks, so it is loud, but it is the kind of loud you can live with.

title: Quiet fidget toys for focus
product: Silicone thumb rocker fidget toys, quiet for classroom
short: A fidget that makes no noise. That is the whole point if a kid needs one at a desk.
intro: I teach, and I have strong opinions about fidgets. The good ones are silent and stay in one hand. The bad ones click, spin, and become the lesson. These are silent.
Video is on the Amazon listing. I show how they feel and why the quiet matters.

title: Scarlett 2i2: seven years in
product: Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 3rd Gen USB audio interface
short: The interface I have recorded voice and piano through for seven years. The video is the tips I wish I had on day one.
intro: Two inputs, one USB cable, and it just works with every mic and every computer I have thrown at it. I have used mine for seven years for vocal coaching recordings, piano, and voice-over.
The video is the stuff I wish somebody had told me on day one, seven years of small lessons in a few minutes.

p: The 3rd gen is what I own and it is still great. The 4th gen adds auto-gain and USB-C. If you are buying new and the price is close, get the 4th gen. If the 3rd gen is on sale, you lose nothing that matters.

title: Scarlett 2i2 4th Gen
product: Focusrite Scarlett 2i2 4th Gen USB-C audio interface
short: The newer version of the interface I use. Auto gain and USB-C are the real upgrades.
intro: Same box, same sound, two upgrades that matter for a beginner: Auto Gain sets your input level for you, and it is USB-C.
Everything in my 2i2 video applies to this one.

title: MAONO PD300X: studio sound over USB
product: MAONO PD300X dynamic microphone, XLR and USB
short: A dynamic mic that plugs straight into USB, no interface needed, and still has XLR for later.
intro: A dynamic mic that sounds like a studio mic, plugs straight into your computer over USB, and also has an XLR jack for when you get an interface. That is the whole pitch and it holds up.
Dynamic means it ignores the room: the fan, the kids, the dog. Good for anyone recording at a kitchen table.

p: It comes with a stand, but you will want a boom arm. Get close to it, two to four inches, and turn the gain up. Dynamic mics are quiet.

title: Why I have 32 OneOdio A71s
product: OneOdio A71 wired over-ear studio headphones
short: The wired headphones I buy for a whole classroom. Cheap, tough, and one feature wins.
intro: I have 32 of these. That is not a joke. When you need headphones for a room full of keyboards or laptops, you need something that sounds decent, survives being dropped, and costs less than a textbook.
The feature that wins for me: a second jack on the earcup, so two people can share one source. In a lesson that is everything.

p: Why I Have 32 of these covers the classroom story. THIS Feature WINS is the shared-jack trick. Both are on the listing.
Wired only. The cable is detachable and replaceable, which is why they last. Red or black.

title: OneOdio Pro 10
product: OneOdio Pro 10 over-ear wired DJ monitor headphones
short: The step-up OneOdio. Bigger drivers, same shared-jack trick.
intro: Same company as the A71, with a 50 mm driver and both a 6.35 mm and 3.5 mm jack on the cord, so they plug into a keyboard or an interface without an adapter.
The daisy-chain feature from my video is here too.

title: Bluetooth headset with a busy light
product: Wireless Bluetooth 5.4 headset with mic and Qualcomm dongle
short: A light on the headset that tells the family you're on a call. Genius.
intro: It is a work headset with a dongle for the laptop, noise cancelling on the mic, and a little red light on the earcup that turns on when you are on a call. Everyone in the house can see it.
If you take calls from home with people in the house, that light is worth it by itself.

title: Streonor S15 stream deck
product: Streonor S15 15-key LCD stream controller, black or white
short: Fifteen little screens you program to do anything. The video shows what I run on mine.
intro: A pad of fifteen buttons with tiny screens. Each one does whatever you set: open an app, mute the mic, run a shortcut, start recording. It is the cheaper cousin of the Stream Deck, and for what I do it is the same thing.
The video shows the workflow I built on it.

p: Comes in black and white. Software is free; give it twenty minutes of setup and it pays you back every day.

title: Turn a laptop into three screens
product: 16-inch 1200P triple portable monitor laptop screen extender
short: Two extra screens that clip onto the laptop and fold flat. My most-watched video for a reason.
intro: It clips onto the back of the laptop and swings out two more screens. Email on one, the gradebook on another, the thing you are actually working on in the middle. Fold it up and it goes in the bag.
This is the video people watch most, and it is the product I get asked about most.

p: Check your laptop size against the listing (this one fits roughly 13 to 17 inch). You need two USB-C ports with video out, or one plus an HDMI. The video shows the cables.

title: Synnov 15.6-inch screen extender
product: Synnov 15.6-inch 1080P triple monitor laptop screen extender
short: The other screen extender I use. Plug in and go.
intro: Same idea as the 16-inch one: two screens that attach to the laptop. This one is a little lighter and a little cheaper.
If you only want one, get whichever is on sale. They both do the job.

title: The coffee mat that makes me look organized
product: Silicone coffee mat, 24 x 16 with tray, deep sea blue
short: A big silicone mat under the espresso machine. Spills stop at the edge and the counter stays clean.
intro: Everything coffee lives on this mat: the Breville, the grinder, the cups. Drips and grounds stay on the mat, and once a week it goes in the sink.
It made my corner of the counter look like a coffee bar instead of a mess.

title: POWRUI outlet extender with night light
product: POWRUI 6-outlet wall extender, 3 USB ports, sensor night light
short: Six outlets and three USB ports from one wall plug, with a night light that turns itself on.
intro: Plug it into the wall and you get six outlets and three USB ports, plus a night light with a sensor so the hallway is lit at 2 a.m. and dark by day.
Bedroom, hallway, or behind the desk.

p: This is a surge protector, so it is for home, not the cruise. For the ship, use the non-surge strip.

title: POWRUI 6-outlet surge protector
product: POWRUI 6-outlet extender, 2 USB-A ports, night light
short: Same POWRUI extender with two USB-A ports instead of three. Usually a bit cheaper.
intro: The slightly older version of the extender in my video. Six outlets, two USB-A ports, same sensor night light.
If you don't need USB-C, this one is fine.

title: Breville Bambino: coffee fast, then save the world
product: Breville Bambino espresso machine, brushed stainless
short: Heats up in three seconds. Real espresso before school. Two videos on the listing.
intro: I wanted real espresso before school without a fifteen-minute warm-up. The Bambino heats in about three seconds, pulls a real shot, and steams milk well enough for a latte.
Two videos: one on the grinder and the Bambino together, one on making coffee fast enough to get out the door.

p: You need a grinder. Pre-ground coffee will not work in an espresso machine. The Smart Grinder Pro is the one I use with it.

title: Breville Smart Grinder Pro
product: Breville BCG820BSS Smart Grinder Pro
short: The grinder that makes the Bambino work. Sixty settings, and you only need to find one.
intro: A burr grinder with sixty settings and a timer so you grind the same dose every morning. It is the half of the espresso setup people skip and then wonder why their shots taste bad.
Video on the listing shows the grinder and the Bambino together.

title: Instant Pot Duo Crisp for busy parents
product: Instant Pot Duo Crisp 8 qt, pressure cooker and air fryer
short: Pressure cooker and air fryer in one pot. The time saver in my video is the steamer basket trick.
intro: One pot that pressure cooks and air fries, so dinner on a school night is thirty minutes instead of an hour. The eight-quart size feeds a family with leftovers.
The video is the time saver: the mesh steamer basket that lets you cook two things at once.

title: Instant Pot mesh steamer basket
product: Instant Pot official stainless mesh steamer basket set
short: The cheap add-on that makes the Instant Pot twice as useful.
intro: Vegetables, eggs, potatoes, dumplings. The basket keeps them out of the liquid and lifts out in one piece. Dishwasher safe.
This is the trick in my Instant Pot video. Buy it with the pot.

title: Sherpa-lined bomber for tricky weather
product: Mega Tshop men's knit fleece bomber jacket, sherpa lined, snap buttons
short: Warm enough for a cold morning, not so warm you sweat by noon.
intro: That stretch of fall where the morning is 40 degrees and the afternoon is 65. Knit outside, sherpa inside, snaps instead of a zipper. It is the jacket I grab on the way to school.
Video on the listing: fit, pockets, how it moves.

title: Lightweight golf jacket for fall and spring
product: Mega Tshop men's brushed zip-up golf jacket, lightweight stretch
short: Thin, stretchy, zips up. The in-between-seasons jacket.
intro: A thin zip-up that stretches when you move. Not for real cold, perfect for 50 and windy. Packs down small enough to live in a bag.
Video shows it on and the fit.

title: Go-to fall fleece jacket
product: Mega Tshop men's full-zip stand-collar fleece jacket with pockets
short: The plain full-zip fleece with a collar and real pockets.
intro: Stand-up collar, full zip, zip pockets. It is the fleece you wear over a t-shirt from October until it snows.
Video on the listing.

title: 100% cotton tee that gets softer
product: Mega Tshop 100% cotton short sleeve t-shirt, regular fit
short: A plain cotton tee that gets better after a few washes instead of worse.
intro: Plain, 100% cotton, regular fit. The thing I like is that it softens with washing and does not twist or shrink weird.
Video on the listing.

title: Color-block tee for any outfit
product: Mega Tshop men's cotton short sleeve color block graphic tee
short: A tee with a little design that still goes with everything.
intro: A step up from a plain tee without being loud. Cotton, holds its shape.
Video on the listing.

title: Soft cotton-blend tee
product: Cotton blend short sleeve t-shirt for men
short: Soft, holds up, works under a jacket or on its own. Yup.
intro: Soft blend, good weight, no shrinking. The kind of shirt you buy three of once you know it fits.
Video on the listing.

title: FIT KING compression boots: my recovery go-to
product: FIT KING cordless air compression leg recovery system, medium
short: Air compression boots for sore legs. Cordless, so you can wear them on the couch.
intro: Legs go in, the boots inflate in sections from the feet up, and twenty minutes later tired legs feel like you took a day off. Cordless, so no sitting next to an outlet.
Two videos on the listing: the first impression and the one after it became a routine.

p: Check sizing against your calf measurement. Medium fit me.

title: See how fast your devices are charging in the car
product: 105W 3-port USB-C car charger with digital display
short: Three ports, 105 watts, and a little screen that shows the watts going out. You learn which cable is bad fast.
intro: A car charger with a screen. The screen shows the wattage going to each port, which is how you find out which of your cables are slow. Three ports means the whole back seat charges.
Video shows it live.

title: Liquid cleaner wax vs paste
product: Car liquid cleaner wax, 10.58 oz
short: Cleans and waxes in one pass. Faster than paste. The video shows the before and after.
intro: One product that cleans light grime and leaves wax behind, so a Saturday wash takes half the time. It will not fix deep scratches. For a car that is just dull, it works.
Video on the listing with the before and after.

title: This speaker hits hard for the size
product: BassBloom Roar 3 portable Bluetooth speaker, 20W, IPX6, 24 hours
short: A small waterproof speaker with real bass. Pool, yard, classroom.
intro: Twenty watts in a speaker you can hold in one hand, waterproof, and the battery runs all day. The bass surprised me, which is why the video exists.
It has RGB lights, which you can turn off.

title: The projector behind a lot of family memories
product: Portable projector (see the listing for the current model name)
short: Movie night on the wall, in the yard, in a hotel room. It has gone everywhere with us.
intro: A projector turned the living room wall into movie night and the side of the house into a backyard theater. The kids ask for it. It has come on trips.
The video is me walking through where we have used it and what to watch for.

p: Brightness matters more than resolution for a family projector. Dark room, white wall, and almost anything looks good. Bring a small Bluetooth speaker; built-in projector speakers are never great.

title: Best all-in-one beard and hair trimmer?
product: Philips Norelco All-in-One 3000, 13-in-1 trimmer
short: One trimmer for beard, hair, and the rest. The 13-in-1 is the one I'd start with.
intro: I compared four Philips trimmers in one video. This is the 13-in-1 and it covers a beard, a haircut at home, and the edges, without buying the 23-piece kit.
Video compares the four side by side.

title: Philips Norelco 9000, 23-in-1
product: Philips Norelco All-in-One 9000, 23-in-1 trimmer, steel
short: The top of the line in my trimmer video. Steel, every attachment, more than most people need.
intro: The steel one with twenty-three attachments. It is the best of the four in my video. It is also the most expensive, and most people will be happy with the 3000.
Buy this if you cut your own hair and want it to last ten years.

title: Philips Norelco Hair Clipper 3000
product: Philips Norelco Hair Clipper 3000, 13 length settings
short: Just a hair clipper. If you only cut hair at home, this is cheaper than the all-in-one.
intro: Not a beard trimmer, just a clipper with thirteen length settings. For buzzing the kids or a simple fade, it is the right tool and it costs less.
Compared in the trimmer video.

title: Philips Multigroom 20-piece set
product: Philips Multigroom all-in-one trimmer, 20 pieces, storage pouch
short: The middle option in my trimmer video. Comes with a pouch, which matters more than it sounds.
intro: Twenty pieces and a pouch to keep them in. If you travel, the pouch is the reason to pick this one over the 3000.
Compared in the trimmer video.

title: Play-Doh Drill 'n Fill dentist
product: Play-Doh Drill 'n Fill Dentist toy, ages 3+
short: The dentist set. Gross in the way a four-year-old loves.
intro: You make teeth, you drill the cavities, you fill them with the metallic Play-Doh. It is a little gross and the kids think that is the best part.
Good for a four- or five-year-old who likes pretend play.

title: Posca paint markers
product: Uni Posca 5M medium acrylic paint markers
short: Paint markers that work on paper, rocks, wood, and sneakers. The art-kid gift.
intro: Paint in a marker. Opaque, bright, and they write on almost anything: paper, rocks, a skateboard, canvas shoes. These are what the art kids ask for by name.
Eight and up, or a crafty adult.

title: Holbein gouache set
product: Holbein Artists' Gouache, set of 12, 5 ml
short: Real artist paint for a kid who has outgrown the washable stuff.
intro: Gouache is opaque watercolor. It dries flat and matte and looks like the illustration in a picture book. Holbein is the real-artist brand, which is the point of the gift.
For a kid who takes art seriously, ten and up.

title: Retrospec Rift longboard
product: Retrospec Rift drop-through longboard, Canadian maple
short: A cruising longboard for a teen who wants to ride, not do tricks.
intro: Drop-through means the deck sits low, so it is stable and easy to push. This is for getting around and carving down a hill, not the skate park.
Twelve and up. Add a helmet.

title: 22-inch mini cruiser skateboard
product: 22-inch mini cruiser retro skateboard
short: The little plastic cruiser. First board for a six- to ten-year-old.
intro: The small plastic board. Light enough for a little kid to carry, soft wheels that roll over cracks, cheap enough that it is fine if they lose interest.
Six to ten years old as a first board.

title: WhiteFang complete skateboard
product: WhiteFang complete skateboard, 31 x 7.88, 7-ply maple
short: A real double-kick skateboard for a kid who wants to learn tricks.
intro: A full-size board with a kick on both ends, so they can learn an ollie. Seven-ply maple, comes assembled.
Eight and up. Helmet, always.

title: Prime Hydration variety pack
product: Prime Hydration drink variety pack, 7 bottles
short: The drink every kid asked for. A variety pack is the gift version.
intro: If you have a kid between eight and fourteen you have heard of Prime. A variety pack lets them try the flavors without committing to twelve of one.
Stocking stuffer level.

title: Prime Hydration Lemonade
product: PRIME Hydration Lemonade, 12-pack
short: The lemonade flavor, 12-pack.
intro: Twelve-pack of the lemonade flavor, for when you already know which one they want.

title: Prime Hydration Glowberry
product: PRIME Hydration Glowberry, 12-pack
short: The Glowberry flavor, 12-pack.
intro: Twelve-pack of Glowberry, the other flavor kids ask for.

title: Wooden chess set
product: Chess Armory 15-inch wooden chess set with storage
short: A real wooden chess set that folds up and holds the pieces. The gift that lasts.
intro: Fifteen-inch folding board, felted pieces, storage inside, extra queens. Chess is the game I would teach every kid, and a nice set makes them want to play.
Six and up with a parent, ten and up alone.

title: Rubik's Cube
product: Rubik's Cube, the original 3x3
short: The original. Every kid should get stuck on one once.
intro: The original 3x3. Watch a ten-minute video on the method and a kid can solve it in a week. Then they can't put it down.
Seven and up.

title: Soft-touch soccer ball
product: Champion Sports Viper soccer ball, sizes 3, 4, 5
short: A soft training ball that doesn't sting when it hits a little kid.
intro: Soft-touch cover, so a six-year-old can head it or take one to the face without crying. Size 3 for under eight, size 4 for eight to twelve, size 5 for teens.
Pump not included; buy one.

title: Clay bead bracelet kit
product: Gionlion 6000 clay beads friendship bracelet making kit, 24 colors
short: Six thousand beads and the kids make bracelets for everyone they know.
intro: Flat clay beads in twenty-four colors, letters, charms, and cord. Hours of quiet, and bracelets for everyone they know.
Six and up. Vacuum afterward.

Stocking stuffer.

title: JBL Flip 5

It will live in their room and then their backpack.

title: LED strip lights for a kid's room

intro: Color-changing LED strips with a remote and an app, and they sync to music. Three hundred feet is enough for the ceiling of a big room with extra.
The gift that makes you the favorite relative.

title: Math for my first grader
product: Spectrum Math Workbook, Grade 1 (Carson Dellosa)
short: The workbook I decided on when my first grader's school stopped sending one home.
intro: My daughter is a great reader. Math is not her strongest suit.
Last year she had a math workbook she worked out of every day, and it helped. This year the school is sending reading home and no math book. So I went looking for one. This is the one I decided on.

p: I compared the ones parents and teachers recommend most: Spectrum, Brain Quest, School Zone Big Math, Math Mammoth, and Math with Confidence.

Spectrum is the closest thing to the workbook a school sends home. Clear pages, one skill at a time, an answer key in the back. It lines up with what a first-grade class actually covers: addition and subtraction, place value, fact families, shapes, and measurement.
Open the Look Inside preview on Amazon and match it to where your kid is right now. There is a pretest at the start of each chapter that helps with that. Ten to twenty minutes a page is about right.

body.h: If this one is not the fit
p: Brain Quest Math 1st Grade is the fun one: stickers, a progress map, activities instead of rows of problems. School Zone Big Math 1-2 is the most pages for the money. Math Mammoth and Math with Confidence are the ones homeschool parents swear by, and they ask more of you as the teacher.
